transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-25
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Rivera (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Mike Patel (CTO - Silvercrest), Elena Ortiz (ML Eng), Ravi Singh (Infra)

Summary (auto): Jordan gave high-level overview of Redwood product family. Main focus was mapping Silvercrest's use cases to model selection and deployment mode. Discussed open models, context window needs, multilingual and function-calling requirements. Action items captured.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, with Samira our SE. Quick intros then jump into your use case.
[00:06] Mike: Hey Jordan, Mike here. We're evaluating options for the new chat assistant we ship to enterprise customers, biggest constraints are latency under load and data residency for some regulated clients.
[00:15] Samira: Great, thanks. Can you walk through current stack? Where are you running inference today?
[00:19] Mike: Right now we use a hybrid 	primary is a hosted API from ClearAI (weird name, not sure) for prototypes, and for clients that require isolation we self-host some models on-prem with a home-grown serving layer. Cost is spiking and ops overhead is high.
[00:31] Elena: Also, we have heavy multilingual requirements 	Spanish and Mandarin mainly 	and we need function/tool calling to connect to our internal ticketing and retrieval system. Retrieval uses Milvus + postgres vectors.
[00:43] Ravi: On infra, our on-prem boxes are A100-ish and some RTX 6000 in colos. We might go Dedicated or Private depending on SLA and network.
[00:51] Jordan: Perfect. So main axes: cost, latency, and compliance. For model selection we usually look at a) open models you can run on Dedicated/Private (Llama2 derivatives, Mistral, Falcon, etc.), b) Redwood-verified variants where we've tuned kernels and quantization, and c) when function-calling + long context needed we map to variants with bigger context windows.
[01:10] Mike: Can you clarify what you mean by Redwood-verified variants?
[01:13] Samira: Yeah, sorry 	we have a catalog of open model builds where our runtime picks optimal kernels, and we provide pre-tested quantization profiles (like 4-bit Q* types) and KV cache handling. That combo often gives 20-40% cost savings vs naive self-hosting. Sometimes the name shows up in docs as 'Redwood-verify' 	auto transcript glitch.
[01:29] Elena: Interesting. On context length 	we have three classes of use: short chat (1-2 turns), medium (multi-turn with 8k context for customer history), and long (up to 60k for session transcripts + retrieval results). What's Redwood's support on 64k?
[01:44] Samira: We support models with extended context, depending on model architecture. For example, we partner with variant builds that can go to 32k and 64k with optimized KV cache and sharded attention kernels. On Hosted it's available for certain tiers, Dedicated can be configured to handle 64k use cases but you'd want to plan capacity because memory grows with context.
[02:03] Mike: And latency impact? If we go 64k for a subset of calls 	 is there a big penalty?
[02:07] Samira: Yes, longer context increases compute per token but our runtime uses continuous batching and prefix caching so if many requests share prefixes (e.g., system prompt + doc snippets) the amortized cost is lower. But single-shot long prompts will increase latency by noticeable amounts 	 we can baseline in pilot.
[02:22] Ravi: For Dedicated vs Private 	 what's the difference operationally? We need KMS and audit logs 	 some clients insist on HSM.
[02:29] Jordan: Dedicated is Redwood-managed physical or virtual capacity isolated to your account with SLA. Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you control over networking and key management; we integrate with customer KMS/HSM and ship audit logs. We also offer an air-gapped package for ultra-regulated customers.
[02:44] Mike: Good. On models: which open models do you recommend for multilingual + tool-calling? We've been testing Mistral Instruct and Llama2-70B but got hallucination in Mandarin.
[02:56] Samira: For multilingual, model choice matters. Llama2-70B variants are solid but need fine-tuning or instruction-tuning for Mandarin. Mistral is strong for instruction in English; Mistral x-high context variants are coming. Falcon-180B has decent multilingual but it's heavy. We usually suggest: 1) For cost-sensitive real-time chat: medium-sized optimized model (e.g., 13B-30B Redwood-optimized) with distillation + quantization. 2) For highest quality multilingual + tool calling: larger 70B+ variants, possibly ensemble with a reranker. 3) For very long context, pick a model architecture that supports block-sparse or sliding window attention 	 we can recommend specific builds.
[03:36] Elena: What about tool-calling/function calling support? We need structured JSON outputs and to call our internal ticketing endpoint.
[03:43] Samira: We support function calling patterns and structured output enforcement. Our runtime can stream tokens with tool-call markers, and you can configure safe-guards. We also recommend a lightweight adapter layer on your side to validate outputs before initiating ticket creation.
[03:56] Mike: Any differences for Hosted vs Dedicated for tool-calling? E.g., webhooks latency?
[04:00] Jordan: Hosted is easiest to get started 	 webhooks, streaming, etc. Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and private networking; webhooks can still be used but for sensitive calls you'd route through your VPC. Private gives you full network control.
[04:13] Ravi: For our pilot, we want to test: 1) latency 95th p95 under load (100 rps), 2) end-to-end tool-call roundtrip with our ticket API, 3) Mandarin QA for extraction accuracy. Can Redwood run that?
[04:26] Samira: Yes, we can allocate a Dedicated pilot or do a Hosted benchmark with similar models. For strict data residency we'll likely do a Dedicated pilot or Private depending on how the audit looks.
[04:37] Mike: Competitors 	 we're also talking to Anthropic and a couple of cloud vendors (Vertex). For pricing, what's stickiest: token costs or dedicated commit?
[04:47] Jordan: Hosted is usage-based (tokens / embed units). Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commit 	 better when you have predictable high throughput. We can show a cost model comparing both given your expected QPS and average token per request.
[04:58] Elena: A question on quantization: does Redwood do 4-bit QLoRA style quant or something else? We worry about quality regressions in Mandarin after heavy quant.
[05:06] Samira: We use per-layer and per-channel quantization profiles tuned per model. For some use cases we recommend mixed-precision or 8-bit for Mandarin-sensitive flows. Part of the pilot is to validate quality/latency tradeoffs. We'll include evals against your prompt set.
[05:20] Mike: Any gotchas with KV cache / multi-tenant noise? We currently see cache thrash when many sessions run.
[05:26] Samira: Our serving runtime does per-customer KV isolation and smart eviction. For Dedicated, you get isolated GPU pools which reduces cross-tenant interference. For Hosted we have tenant isolation policies and quotas.
[05:38] Ravi: On the infra side, can Redwood's private deployment integrate with our on-prem K8s + existing GPUs?
[05:44] Samira: Yes, Private supports on-prem packaging and we provide deployment manifests for K8s; we also have a managed option where Redwood helps set up the control plane. We'll send the ops doc.
[05:53] Mike: Let's talk about timeline. We want a pilot in 2 weeks and production in 2 months if results look good. Is that feasible?
[05:59] Jordan: Feasible. We'll need your prompts and a sense of expected traffic shape. We'll send a pricing + sizing proposal in 48 hours and propose pilot slots.
[06:08] Elena: For the pilot model list 	 can you include Llama2-70B Redwood-optimized, Mistral-instruct variant, Falcon-180B-lr, and a 13B optimized baseline for cost comparison?
[06:18] Samira: Yes, we'll prepare that. We'll also include quantization profiles and expected token/sec at p95 for each model.
[06:24] Mike: Ok. Any security items we should expect in the SOC2 pack? SSO, RBAC, audit log retention?
[06:30] Jordan: SOC2, SAML SSO integrations, role-based access controls, audit logs, and KMS integration are all covered. We'll attach the security pack and a short FAQ on Private deployment controls.
[06:39] Ravi: One more 	 we might need HSM certs for a subset of customers. You mentioned HSM earlier?
[06:44] Jordan: Yes, we integrate with customer HSM for key storage on Private deployments; we can detail cert exchange.
[06:50] Mike: Cool. Let's recap next steps 	 send pricing, security docs, model perf spreadsheet, customer to send prompt set, and schedule pilot.
[06:58] Jordan: Sounds good. We'll send items and book pilot slots. Thanks everyone.
[07:03] Mike: Thanks, bye.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions: 'Redwood-verify' instead of Redwood-verified; 'KV cash' typo in one segment. There was slight crosstalk during the latency discussion.

End of transcript.
